settings.brandLine: Precision Before, During and Beyond Construction.

capabilities.text: coordinating multidisciplinary models so conflicts are found and resolved before construction
prioritising critical issues and driving them to closure with clear ownership
coordinating project information so site teams work from resolved, consistent drawings
providing independent model QA/QC and delivery assurance that keeps risks and records visible
supporting internal BIM and design teams when they are overloaded

exposures.label: paid-for installation removed and repeated
exposures.consequence: a structural or services interface found only after installation can mean removing work that has already been paid for and repeating it
exposures.stake: That cost sits on top of the original price and comes straight out of the package margin.
exposures.prevention: closing those interfaces in the coordinated model before packages reach site

exposures.label: wasted purchased and fabricated material
exposures.consequence: material ordered or fabricated against drawings that still hold an open coordination issue can arrive on site unusable
exposures.stake: The spend is already committed, and replacement orders bring their own lead times.
exposures.prevention: confirming that coordination is closed before materials are ordered or fabricated

exposures.label: crews, plant and subcontractors standing idle
exposures.consequence: a crew can arrive ready to install and find the area blocked by an unresolved interface, while labour, plant and subcontractors stay on the clock
exposures.stake: Work stops, but the cost of the resources does not.
exposures.prevention: releasing work packages only once their interfaces are resolved

exposures.label: programme slippage, prolongation and subcontractor claims
exposures.consequence: one late design conflict on a critical package can push the programme and open the door to prolongation and subcontractor claims
exposures.stake: Time-related costs grow every week the issue stays open.
exposures.prevention: keeping critical-path interfaces visible and closed ahead of construction

exposures.label: margin reduction and contract disputes
exposures.consequence: an unresolved technical decision can turn into a variation dispute over who pays for the change
exposures.stake: Even when the position is defensible, the argument consumes margin and management time.
exposures.prevention: recording and closing technical decisions before they become commercial disputes

exposures.label: known issues left open without an owner
exposures.consequence: an interface raised in design meetings but never assigned to an owner can still be open when construction reaches it
exposures.stake: The contractor may then claim time and cost, and the client will ask the project management team why the risk stayed open.
exposures.prevention: keeping issue ownership and closure visible until each critical issue is resolved

exposures.label: late or conflicting project information
exposures.consequence: late or conflicting drawing revisions can leave the contractor working from information the design team has already superseded
exposures.stake: The resulting rework and requests for information land on the project manager's desk.
exposures.prevention: making sure every team works from coordinated, current information

exposures.label: poor risk visibility in client reporting
exposures.consequence: technical risks that never reach the client report can surface later as a cost or time surprise
exposures.stake: That kind of surprise damages client confidence faster than the issue itself.
exposures.prevention: making technical risk visible and current in client reporting

exposures.label: weak records complicating approvals, payment or handover
exposures.consequence: unresolved technical issues or incomplete records can delay approvals, payment certificates or handover
exposures.stake: Cash flow and the contractual position both suffer while the gaps are chased.
exposures.prevention: keeping coordination records complete enough to support approvals and handover

exposures.label: loss of client confidence and future appointments
exposures.consequence: a coordination failure that reaches site can be remembered by the client long after the project closes
exposures.stake: For a consultancy, that can cost the next appointment rather than one project's fee.
exposures.prevention: protecting delivery quality so issues are closed before the client sees them
